definitions.explanation: A fraction whose numerator is equal to or larger than its denominator, so that its value is 1 or more — for example 5/3. It can always be rewritten as a {帯分数|たいぶんすう} (mixed number).

examples.japanese: 3{分|ぶん}の5は{仮分数|かぶんすう}だ。
{仮分数|かぶんすう}を{帯分数|たいぶんすう}に{直|なお}しなさい。
examples.english: Convert the improper fraction into a mixed number.

examples.japanese: かけ{算|ざん}や{割|わ}り{算|ざん}をするときは、{帯分数|たいぶんすう}より{仮分数|かぶんすう}のほうが{計算|けいさん}しやすい。
examples.english: When multiplying or dividing, improper fractions are easier to work with than mixed numbers.

notes:
{仮|か} (provisional, temporary) + {分数|ぶんすう} (fraction): a fraction only in form, since its value is not less than one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仮分数|かぶんすう}に{直|なお}す: to convert into an improper fraction
- {仮分数|かぶんすう}で{答|こた}える: to give the answer as an improper fraction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {真分数|しんぶんすう}: proper fraction — numerator smaller than the denominator
- {帯分数|たいぶんすう}: mixed number — the same value written as a whole number plus a fraction
- {分数|ぶんすう}: fraction — the general term
